text:
Jack Quinn picked a good season to break out. The Athletic has called his next contract Buffalo's most intriguing negotiation, and he has answered with nine goals and 16 points in 17 games. The role changed first: 19:05 a night, up three and a half minutes, and on the ice for 83% of the Sabres' power play, up from 37%.

Part of it is earned. His own chances are up to 1.16 expected goals per 60 from 0.96, and his last ten games produced 12 points against about 9 we'd expect. Part of it isn't: he is shooting 20%, double last season, against a normal range of roughly 11 to 15%.

The question that will matter in negotiations is defense. Evolving-Hockey had him at replacement level last season, largely because opponents got a lot more with him on (bottom 2% of forwards). Buffalo is winning his minutes at five-on-five this year, 54% of the expected goals. Our projection says about 32 goals, which would make that contract expensive.
headline: Quinn's contract year is going loud
